recent_posts.title: Pretext vs. Traditional Layout in 2026: Is the DOM Finally Obsolete?
recent_posts.summary: Pretext is a pure JavaScript text measurement library that performs layout calculations outside the browser's main rendering cycle, eliminating DOM reflows. It claims sub-millisecond layout performance and full i18n support. A community gallery called the Pretext Wall showcases demos like dynamic text reflow, shrink-wrap chat bubbles, and typographic ASCII art that would be impractical with traditional DOM-based layout approaches.

recent_posts.title: Learning React First Is Actually a Mistake
recent_posts.summary: Learning React before mastering JavaScript fundamentals and browser mechanics is counterproductive. React is an abstraction over the DOM, state management, and event-driven programming — concepts that must be understood first to use React effectively. Beginners who skip straight to React end up cargo-culting patterns without understanding why they work, and their JS knowledge gaps get hidden until they cause production bugs. A better learning path: solid JavaScript first, then browser/DOM fundamentals, then build a small app without any framework, and only then adopt React. Frameworks change, but mental models built on fundamentals last.

recent_posts.title: No-Code Is Dying And Honestly, It’s About Time.
recent_posts.summary: No-code platforms are evolving from simple drag-and-drop tools into sophisticated development engines that complement rather than replace traditional coding. Modern no-code tools now offer custom databases, API integrations, advanced workflows, and extensibility through code blocks, making them valuable productivity multipliers for developers building internal tools, prototypes, and automation layers. The integration of AI assistants is accelerating this transformation, enabling both technical and non-technical users to build faster while blurring the lines between no-code and low-code development.

recent_posts.title: Tired of setting up Vite + React + Tailwind again and again?

recent_posts.title: Fira Code iScript, to make reading code faster
recent_posts.summary: Fira Code iScript is a font variation that combines Fira Code's regular and bold styles with Script12 italics to improve code readability. The font maintains ASCII compatibility, supports IDE ligatures, and uses visual symbols to replace common programming sequences like arrows and comparison operators, helping developers read code faster with reduced cognitive load.

recent_posts.title: How I’m using AI to manage tasks, research, and notes in Notion

The tool aims to solve common productivity pain points like buried tasks and time-consuming research by providing seamless Notion integration, automated research capabilities, simplified task prioritization, and instant image search functionality.

recent_posts.title: Making system design diagrams less painful.

recent_posts.title: How Dynamic URLs Help You Test Content at Scale
recent_posts.summary: Dynamic URLs enable on-the-fly media transformations through URL parameters, allowing teams to create multiple variants of images and videos from a single file. This approach eliminates the need to generate and store multiple versions, enabling faster experimentation with resizing, cropping, filtering, and text overlays without requiring file uploads or developer intervention.
